title: Evidence dehydration & rehydration playbook and operator notes
body:
Purpose:
This playbook documents the staging format, operator workflows, and emergency procedures for the evidence dehydration and rehydration pipeline used by Redwood's security evidence collectors. It complements the collector-sidecar and SIEM export specs by defining a compact, tamper-evident artifact format for long-term storage and fast on-demand reconstruction for audits or incident forensics.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: SREs, security engineers, SOC operators, compliance reviewers, and on-call operators who may need to rehydrate evidence for an audit or incident.
- Scope: Collector output packaging, checksum and proof metadata, storage lifecycle, RBAC controls for read/restore, SIEM export mappings from rehydrated artifacts, backfill and replay procedures. Not in scope: collector instrumentation internals, SIEM ingestion pipeline implementation (covered in separate spec).

High-level concepts:
- Dehydration: transforming verbose event/evidence payloads into a compact, encoded archive that includes minimal replay metadata and cryptographic integrity metadata. Primary goal is storage efficiency and long-term tamper evidence while keeping rehydration fast.
- Rehydration: reconstructing the original event payloads and per-record audit headers required for SIEM exports or control evidence review.
- Proof bundle: a JSON-lite sidecar with hashes, sequence anchors, and signing metadata used to verify integrity and chain-of-custody.
- Index shard: smaller index files mapping compacted offsets to original request ids and timestamps to support quick lookups without full rehydration.

Dehydration format (operator-friendly summary):
Each dehydrated object is a gzipped tar of three files: payloads.lz4 (concatenated, LZ4-compressed binary blobs), index.jsonl (newline JSON with record_id, offset, length, timestamp, schema_version), and proof.json (hashes + signer metadata). File naming: evidence-<collector>-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ.dehyd.tar.gz
Fields in index.jsonl (one per line):
- record_id: stable uuid v4 assigned at collection time
- offset: byte offset into payloads.lz4
- length: length of the compressed blob
- ts: RFC3339 timestamp of the original event
- schema: audit schema version (e.g., audit-v2.1)
- mutability: immutable | ttl-expirable | ephemeral (guides retention enforcement)
Proof.json fields:
- bundle_hash: sha256 of the whole tar.gz (base64)
- index_hash: sha256 of index.jsonl (base64)
- first_record_ts / last_record_ts (RFC3339)
- signer: service account id that issued the bundle (format: svc-evidence@redwood-inference)
- signature: base64-ed25519(signature(bundle_hash) by signer key)
- proof_version: e.g., 1.0

Storage and retention rules (summary):
- Primary hot store: evidence-bucket/hot/YYYY/MM/DD/ for last 14 days, immediate rehydration allowed.
- Cold store: evidence-bucket/cold/YYYY/ for 365-day retention; proofs retained for 2 years.
- Immutable lock: once proof.signature is present, the object is immutable and may only be deleted by an approved retention-manager role through an audited flow.
- TTL annotations in index.jsonl are enforced by the retention worker; mutability flag determines whether partial deletions are permitted.

RBAC v2 controls for evidence artifacts and operations:
Define roles (examples):
- evidence-reader: read-only access to cold/hot objects, cannot request rehydration. Intended for auditors and compliance reviewers.
- evidence-operator: can trigger rehydration jobs and view rehydrated artifacts in ephemeral store, cannot sign bundles.
- evidence-admin: manage retention policies, approve deletions, rotate signer keys.
- evidence-signer: service role used only by automation to sign dehydrated bundles.
Access rules and constraints:
- Rehydration requests must include a justification string and Jira/Linear ticket id; this is logged to the audit pipeline and appended to rehydration.proof.json when completed.
- evidence-operator requests produce an ephemeral artifact with a 48-hour TTL and are written to a separate ephemeral-s3 prefix with access restricted by pre-signed URLs tied to id tokens.

Audit log schema for dehydration/rehydration operations (fields we care about):
- event_type: dehydration_job | rehydration_job | deletion_request | retention_change
- job_id: stable uuid for the operator action
- actor: principal id (svc or user)
- target_bundle: object name
- request_ts: RFC3339
- result: success | partial | failed
- error_code: optional short code
- justification_ticket: optional
- proof_snapshot: bundle_hash (so audits can reference proof without copying large artifacts)
Sample line (JSON):
{"event_type":"rehydration_job","job_id":"c1f3a9b2-...","actor":"samira@redwood.com","target_bundle":"evidence-kiosk-20250112T153000Z.dehyd.tar.gz","request_ts":"2025-01-12T15:34:05Z","result":"success","justification_ticket":"JIRA-SEC-7890","proof_snapshot":"n9x..."}

SIEM export considerations for rehydrated events:
- Rehydration produces normalized events (audit-v2.1) that must be mapped to SIEM fields used by SOC. Sample mapping guidance:
  - audit.request_id -> siem.event_id
  - audit.principal -> siem.user_id
  - audit.action -> siem.action
  - audit.resource -> siem.target
  - audit.ts -> siem.timestamp
- Include proof.bundle_hash in siem.event_meta.proof_hash for cross-referencing back to stored artifacts.
- Tag rehydrated exports with automation_source = "rehydration" to prevent double-counting with live streams.

Collector behavior and resilience notes (operator tips):
- Collectors must flush rotating buffers to an in-memory chunker every 30s or when chunk size > 10MB. This chunker writes compressed blobs into payloads.lz4 and appends index lines atomically.
- In the event of partial writes (process crash), the maintenance worker will attempt to reconstruct index.jsonl from trailing checksums and create a repair proof (signed) that documents repair actions. Repaired bundles must include repaired:true in proof.json and must be manually reviewed by evidence-admin before rotation to cold store.

Backfill and replay plan (for incidents or audits):
1) Create backfill ticket and attach justification and time window. 2) evidence-operator triggers backfill job with time window and target collector(s). 3) System identifies matching dehydrated bundles and queues rehydration. 4) Rehydration runs in parallel with max concurrency parameter controlled by dedicated capacity quotas. 5) Generated normalized events are pushed to ephemeral export prefix and a rehydration manifest is appended to the job audit log.
Notes: backfills over 30 days require evidence-admin approval and additional cost analysis.

Emergency restore procedure (short):
- If SIEM needs immediate historical context, call pager on-call SRE and request expedited rehydration with priority flag. Expedited jobs bypass cold store retrieval TTLs but require an evidence-admin temporary elevated token and will be fully logged and require post-incident review.

Monitoring, alerts, and SLOs:
- Dehydration success rate >= 99.5% (30-day rolling). Alert: >0.5% failures in 1 hour.
- Rehydration job median wall-time for 1GB bundle: < 90s in hot store (SLO). Alert if median > 5 mins for 1GB.
- Proof signature validation failures: immediate P1 incident.

Operator CLI snippets (examples):
- List bundles: rwd-evidence ls --prefix hot/2025/01/12 --limit 200
- Trigger rehydration: rwd-evidence rehydrate --bundle evidence-auth-20250112T153000Z.dehyd.tar.gz --ticket JIRA-SEC-7890 --reason "SOC request"
- Inspect proof: rwd-evidence verify --bundle ./evidence-... --show-proof

Open questions / TODOs:
- Agree on final proof signature rotation cadence (current proposal: quarterly for signer keys).
- Decide safe maximum backfill window for self-serve evidence-operators without evidence-admin oversight.
- Add integration test that runs full dehydr->rehydrate->siem-export for an end-to-end audit.

References and contacts:
- Primary owner: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood-inference.com)
- On-call SRE: see oncall rota in Confluence page: confluence://ops/oncall
- Related specs: collector-sidecar pattern (confluence://sec/collector-sidecar), SIEM mapping doc (confluence://soc/siem-mapping-v1)

Appendix: quick checklist for launching a rehydration request:
- [ ] Create ticket and include justification + reviewer
- [ ] Confirm bundle name(s) and time window
- [ ] Run rwd-evidence verify against bundle(s)
- [ ] Trigger rehydration with --ticket flag
- [ ] Attach resulting rehydration manifest to the ticket and mark for compliance review

End of playbook.
